title: Fish, tilapia, baked or broiled, coated

content.title: About
content.content: Tilapia is a freshwater fish from the Cichlidae family, widely farmed in aquaculture. The fillet has a mild flavor, white color, and tender texture. Baking or broiling retains most nutrients, while a coating adds a crisp crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tilapia is one of the fastest‑growing farmed fish species, with a production cycle of 6‑9 months.
Coatings are often made from whole‑grain flour, breadcrumbs, or nut crumbs, increasing fiber content.
Tilapia adapts to a range of water conditions, including fresh and slightly brackish water.
In the United States, tilapia is commonly called “white fish” and is used in many international cuisines.
Baking at 180‑200 °C preserves up to 90 % of vitamin B12.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Tilapia fillet provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: It contains less than 2 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The fish is high in vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which aid nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Tilapia supplies phosphorus, selenium and potassium, important for bones, antioxidant protection and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Moderate omega‑3
items.content: Although lower than fatty fish, tilapia still contributes omega‑3 fatty acids that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Water quality control
items.content: Aquaculture may involve antibiotics and chemicals; choose products from reputable sources.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Tilapia generally has low mercury levels, but total heavy‑metal intake should be considered with high consumption.

items.title: High‑salt coatings
items.content: Pre‑made coatings can be salty; check the label and rinse if necessary.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tilapia fillets can be baked for 15‑20 minutes at 180‑200 °C, grilled, or steamed. Before baking, the fillet is often coated with breadcrumbs, spices and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve with vegetable sides, lemon wedges or a light yogurt‑based sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh tilapia in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, sealed in an airtight bag, for up to 2 days. Frozen fillets store at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw frozen fish in the fridge, not at room temperature.
